evidence.text:
Reason for referral: Evaluation of intermittent palpitations in a patient with paroxysmal
atrial fibrillation.
Most recent echo showed an ejection fraction of 30%.

Findings: Normal left ventricular size. Left ventricular ejection fraction estimated at
55%. Mild left atrial enlargement. No pericardial effusion.
Impression: Normal left ventricular systolic function.

Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth once daily
Levothyroxine 50 mcg by mouth once daily
Warfarin 5 mg by mouth once daily

EXAM:
General: alert, no acute distress.
Neck: no carotid bruits.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, no murmurs or gallops.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: trace ankle edema.

EXAM:
General: well appearing, no distress.
Neck: no carotid bruits.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, grade 2/6 systolic ejection
murmur, no radiation.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: no peripheral edema.
